sourceEvidence.claim: Uploads were persisted and dispatched without malware content scanning.
Untrusted files entered native conversion parsers.
Outputs and ZIP archives were served without a release scan.
The application ran as root with a broad read-write data mount and no scanner service.
Clamd supports streamed INSTREAM scans; its TCP protocol is unauthenticated and unencrypted.
Non-root execution, reduced capabilities and isolation reduce container compromise impact.
TrueNAS recommends least privilege and restricted service/share exposure.
The target revision pinned vulnerable upload, framework, remote-download and frontend build dependencies.
Remote URLs had no private-address policy or remote byte ceiling.

options.title: Validation and parser updates only
options.summary: Retain extension/family validation, reject unsupported files and keep converter packages current.

tradeoffs.securityEffect: Reduces accidental incompatibility but does not detect known malware or malicious output.
tradeoffs.availability: No scanner dependency and lowest latency.
tradeoffs.operability: Simple, but parser patching must be consistently prompt.
tradeoffs.deliveryRisk: Low implementation risk but leaves the primary file-borne threat untreated.

options.residualRisk: Known malware, weaponized documents and compromised output remain releasable.

options.title: Dedicated fail-closed ClamAV admission and release gate
options.summary: Stream every input and output to an isolated non-root clamd service, block on findings or incomplete scans, and harden all containers.
options.controlOwnership: API owns upload/release gates; worker owns pre-parser/output gates; ClamAV owns signature detection; TrueNAS owns host containment and recovery.

tradeoffs.securityEffect: Blocks known malware at each material boundary and limits scanner/parser compromise impact.
tradeoffs.availability: Fail-closed behavior makes scanner health a dependency; clean output remains available for retry after transient release-scan failure.
tradeoffs.performance: Each file is streamed multiple times and ClamAV requires roughly 2-3 GiB RAM for large-file scanning.
tradeoffs.operability: Requires signature-volume monitoring, scanner health checks and an additional local image.
tradeoffs.cost: Consumes additional memory, CPU and initial signature-download bandwidth.
tradeoffs.deliveryRisk: Moderate rollout risk because existing data must be writable by UID/GID 10001 and ClamAV needs first-start warm-up time.

options.residualRisk: Unknown malware, parser zero-days, application-level abuse and a compromised worker's access to MediaForge data remain.
